_readme: Recipes offered to the app under Recipes -> Recipe library. See RECIPES.md for the schema. Adding an entry here and pushing to main is all it takes: GitHub Pages redeploys and the phone sees it on the next open. An entry on a branch is not published until that branch reaches main.

recipes.name: Salt rolls
recipes.ingredients:
TANGZHONG
20g bread flour
50g whole milk
50g water

DOUGH
330g bread flour
7g instant yeast
35g sugar
6g fine sea salt
100g whole milk, lukewarm
1 egg + 1 yolk, room temperature
55g unsalted European butter, softened

PAN AND TOPPING
30g butter, melted, for the pan
30g butter, melted, for brushing after
Flaky Maldon salt
recipes.steps:
1. Tangzhong. Whisk flour, milk and water in a small pan over medium-low heat 2-3 min to a thick paste. Cool 5 min to lukewarm.

2. Dough. Combine flour, sugar, salt and yeast. Add milk, egg, yolk and the tangzhong. Mix low 2 min, then medium-low 5 min. Add butter a tablespoon at a time, then knead 8-10 min to the windowpane test.

3. First rise. Oiled bowl, covered. Use the Proof dough recipe: 80F at 60% humidity, about 60 min, until doubled.

4. Shape. Butter the pan with 30g melted butter. Divide into 9 pieces of 70-75g, roll each tight, arrange 3x3.

5. Second proof on the counter, covered, 45-60 min, while the oven and steel heat. Pull it slightly under-proofed - puffy, not fully doubled.

6. Bake. Send this recipe with the baking steel on rack 2. It soaks the steel for 45 min, then holds. Set the pan on the steel and press start on the oven.

7. Finish. Brush with the remaining 30g melted butter the moment they come out, scatter Maldon salt, rest 10 min in the pan.
recipes.notes:
2026-09-05 bake: good crumb, but the bottom was not crisp and the top was overcooked. Cause was the rear element - convection at 375F for 20+ min browns the crowns. This version drops it: bottom element only for the long middle, colour from a short top+bottom finish, and a preheated steel under the pan for the base.

Next time: check colour at the start of stage 4 and cut it short if they are already there. Target 195-200F internal (needs the probe).

recipes.name: Pork ragù over creamy polenta
recipes.ingredients:
PORK
3 pounds skinless, boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 3 pieces
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon vegetable oil
1 large onion, finely chopped
6 garlic cloves, finely chopped
2 tablespoons tomato paste
½ cup full-bodied red wine
1 28-ounce can whole peeled tomatoes
4 sprigs thyme
2 sprigs rosemary
2 bay leaves

POLENTA AND ASSEMBLY
Kosher salt
1½ cups coarse polenta (not quick-cooking)
¼ cup unsalted butter
½ cup grated Parmesan (from about 2 ounces), plus more for serving
Freshly ground black pepper
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
Olive oil (for drizzling)
recipes.steps:
1. Season pork with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large heavy pot over medium. Cook pork, turning often, until evenly browned, 10-12 minutes. Transfer to a platter and pour off pan drippings.

2. Wipe out any burned bits from pot, but leave the golden-brown pieces (doing this will keep the finished sauce from tasting bitter). Add onion and garlic to pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is starting to brown and caramelize, 12-15 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly darkened in color, 5-8 minutes.

3. Add wine and cook, scraping up any browned bits, until reduced by about half, 5-8 minutes.

4. Add tomatoes, crushing with your hands as you go, then add thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves; stir in 2 cups water. Add pork with any juices accumulated on the platter; season with salt and pepper.

5. Bring liquid to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, until pork is falling-apart tender, sauce is thickened (it will be thicker than a typical pasta sauce), and flavors have melded, 2-3 hours.

6. Using 2 forks, break up pork into pieces or shred it (your choice); taste and season with salt and pepper.

7. Pork can be cooked 5 days ahead. Let cool; cover and chill in sauce.

8. Bring 6 cups salted water to a boil in a large pot. Whisking constantly, gradually add polenta; reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, whisking often, until polenta is tender and creamy, 20-25 minutes (if polenta becomes too thick too soon, loosen mixture by adding more water and continue cooking). Add butter and ½ cup Parmesan to polenta and whisk until melted; season with salt and pepper.

9. Spoon polenta into bowls or onto a platter and top with pork. Scatter parsley and more Parmesan over top and drizzle with oil.
recipes.notes:
Marked “Excellent!!” on the printout.

Step 5 is the long one: 2½–3 hours simmering. The printed recipe says 2½–3; the timer here offers 3 so it does not go off early.

Nothing in this uses the oven — it is stovetop from start to finish.

recipes.name: Miso and soy Chilean sea bass
recipes.ingredients:
MARINADE
1/2 cup white miso
1/2 cup sake
1/2 cup mirin
1/4 cup soy sauce
1/3 cup packed brown sugar

FISH
1.78 lb Chilean sea bass, one skin-on piece, frozen
2 tablespoons neutral oil, for the pans
2 scallions, greens sliced, to finish
recipes.steps:
1. Thaw. Move the fish from the freezer to the fridge the night before — a 1.78 lb piece wants a good 12 to 14 hours. In the fridge, not on the counter, and do not refreeze it once thawed.

2. Portion while it is still icy at the core, an hour or so before it is fully thawed. Thawed sea bass is soft and fatty and cuts raggedly; semi-frozen it slices clean. Cut 5 pieces of about 160g. The fillet tapers, so cut the thin end wide and the thick end narrow — even out the thickness, not the width, because thickness is what decides when each piece is done.

3. Whisk the miso, sake, mirin, soy sauce and brown sugar together until the miso and the sugar have dissolved. Put the portions in a large resealable bag, pour it over, seal and chill 3 to 6 hours.

4. Wipe the fillets nearly clean before they touch the pan. This is the step that decides the dish — that much sugar and miso solids scorch in about ninety seconds. Then pat them dry: previously frozen fish holds extra water, and surface water is what makes a pan spit.

5. Sear. Neutral oil, medium heat rather than high, across two pans so nothing is crowded. Skin down 4 to 5 minutes, then flip for 2 to 3. The thick loin pieces want the long end of both, the tail end the short.

6. While they cook, pour about half the reserved marinade into a small pan with a splash of water, bring it to a full boil, and reduce 3 to 4 minutes to a syrup that coats a spoon. It has held raw fish, so it needs a real boil rather than a warm-through. Discard the other half.

7. Spoon the glaze over the fillets off the heat and scatter the scallion greens.
recipes.notes:
Stovetop on purpose. The oven version of this finished at 482F under the top element — oily fish, high radiant heat, close to the element, which is the splatter the Anova gets avoided for. It also wanted the oven at the same time as the Salt rolls.

MARINADE TIMING. 3 to 6 hours is the window. This is a salty marinade and past about 12 hours it starts to cure rather than season — firmer flesh, too salty. If the schedule forces an overnight soak, pull the fish out in the morning, pat it dry and keep it covered in the fridge; the flavour is already in and taking it out stops the cure.

PORTIONS. 1.78 lb is about 807g, so 5 portions of roughly 160g. Generous for a fish this rich. The marinade here is scaled about 1.5x from the 4-portion original, with the soy held back slightly rather than scaled straight up, since it sits on the fish for hours.

TIMING WITH THE SALT ROLLS. The rolls rest 10 minutes in the pan after they come out, and this is about 8 minutes of searing plus the glaze. Start the fish when the rolls come out. Note it wants three burners — two for the fish, one for the glaze — so clear the stove first.

IF YOU WANT IT EASIER. The same flavours simmered nitsuke-style make almost no mess and are far more forgiving of uneven portions: 3/4 cup sake, 3/4 cup water, 4 tablespoons mirin, 3 tablespoons soy, 1 1/2 tablespoons brown sugar and ginger coins brought to a bare simmer, fish in skin-side up under a round of parchment laid on the liquid, 9 to 10 minutes for thick pieces. Lift the fish out, whisk 3 tablespoons miso in off the heat, reduce to a glaze. No browning, but the flavour goes all the way through.

recipes.name: Ultimate banana nut bread
recipes.ingredients:
565g bananas, 4 medium, ripe but not fully black (about 340g peeled)
115g plain Greek yogurt, preferably nonfat
2 large eggs, straight from the fridge
15g vanilla extract (1 tablespoon)
280g all-purpose flour
150g sugar, preferably toasted
85g oat flour, such as Bob's Red Mill
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon baking soda
3g Diamond Crystal kosher salt (3/4 teaspoon; for table salt use half the volume)
3/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
1/4 teaspoon ground or grated nutmeg
150g coconut oil, virgin or refined, creamy but firm, about 70F
170g toasted pecan or other nut pieces
Banana whipped cream, optional, to serve
recipes.steps:
1. Line a 10.5 x 5.5 inch loaf pan with a 9 x 13 inch sheet of parchment. Two 9 x 5 inch pans also work, lined with 7 x 13 inch sheets.

2. Peel the bananas and mash them with the Greek yogurt, eggs and vanilla in a medium bowl. If the bananas are underripe, cover the bowl and let the mixture stand 30 minutes.

3. Combine the flour, sugar, oat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and coconut oil in the bowl of a stand mixer with the paddle. Mix on low until the coconut oil disappears into a mealy powder.

4. Add the banana mash and mix only until the floury bits disappear. Fold in the nuts with a spatula, scrape into the pan and spread level. Set it on rack 2, low-middle.

5. Send this recipe. Stage 1 bakes 45 minutes at 350F on the top and bottom elements. Stage 2 drops the top element for the last 25 minutes so the centre finishes without the crown darkening further.

6. It is done when it is well risen and golden brown, and about 206F in the middle. Seventy minutes total is the recipe's own figure for a large loaf; two small loaves want about 45.

7. Wrapped tightly in foil it keeps 3 days at room temperature or a week in the fridge.
recipes.notes:
Stella Parks. The oat flour and the Greek yogurt are what keep the crumb moist, and the cinnamon-cloves-nutmeg blend is there to amplify the banana rather than to taste of spice. Do not drop them for a plainer loaf without expecting a different bread.

206F internal is the real doneness test and the probe is broken, so the 45/25 split is a stand-in for it. Check with an instant-read at the end of stage 2 before pulling it.

No rear element anywhere in this. Seventy minutes under convection would brown the crown long before the middle reached 206F -- the Salt rolls problem, over a much longer bake. Top and bottom for the first 45 is an ordinary home oven, which is what the recipe assumes; bottom only for the last 25 is the foil tent done with elements.

Bottom-element-only caps at 356F, so stage 2 has almost no headroom. Do not raise the temperature without turning the top element back on.

Vent opens on stage 2 to dry the surface. If the crust comes out tougher than you like, close it.

Rack 2 is my read of the recipe's 'lower-middle'. I still do not know which end of the 1-5 scale is the top, so check the first bake and correct this line.

Muffin variant from the source: divide the batter among 12 greased nonstick cups, about 120g each, and bake until domed and just browning at the edges, about 25 minutes. That is one stage, not two -- it is too short to need the split.

recipes.name: Jagerschnitzel, American style
recipes.ingredients:
PORK
5 boneless pork loin cutlets, about 5 oz each
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

BREADING
1 cup all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, for the flour
3 large eggs
2 tablespoons whole milk
2 cups fine dry breadcrumbs

FRYING
2 cups neutral oil or clarified butter, enough for 1/3 inch in the pan
2 tablespoons unsalted butter
1 lemon, in wedges
recipes.steps:
1. Start the oven first. Send this recipe: it heats to 200F and holds there. The app will say it is waiting for a press on the oven panel — you never need to press it. The holding is the whole point, and it is where the fried cutlets wait while you work through the batches.

2. Pound the cutlets between two sheets of plastic to a scant 1/4 inch. This is the dish. Thin and even matters more than anything else here — a cutlet that varies in thickness cooks unevenly no matter what you do afterwards. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

3. Set up three dishes: the flour with the 1/2 teaspoon salt, the eggs beaten with the milk, and the breadcrumbs. Flour each cutlet and shake off the excess, then egg, letting it drip, then crumbs.

4. Lay the crumbs on and press only just enough to make them stick. Do not pack them down. A loose coat is what lets the crust puff and blister away from the meat; a pressed one goes dense and flat.

5. Heat 1/3 inch of oil in a wide skillet to 340-350F with a tablespoon of the butter in it. Use two pans if you want this over faster.

6. Fry two at a time, 2 to 3 minutes a side, to deep golden. As each side cooks, tilt the pan and spoon the hot fat over the top. That basting is what makes the crust lift — it is the difference between schnitzel and a breaded pork chop.

7. Lift each one onto a rack, salt it immediately, and slide the rack into the 200F oven. Onto a rack, not paper towels — paper traps steam and the underside goes soft in a couple of minutes.

8. Serve with the mushroom gravy and lemon wedges, spatzle alongside. Put the gravy under the schnitzel or in a jug, not poured over the top: that crust took real work and sauce softens it within a minute.
recipes.notes:
Breaded, with gravy over it, is the American version and it is what goes with the Jager gravy. Worth knowing that in Germany Jagerschnitzel is usually an unbreaded cutlet — the breaded-plus-sauce combination is largely a restaurant and US habit. Not wrong, just not the original, and it is why the serving note about keeping the sauce off the crust matters more here than it would in Germany.

THE OVEN STAGE is only a warm hold: 200F, rear element, vent open. The open vent is the point — it lets the steam coming off five fried cutlets escape instead of collecting and softening the crust, and the fan keeps air moving over them. It holds indefinitely, so send it before you start pounding. If they will sit longer than about 30 minutes, drop it to 175F; thin pork dries out.

CRUMBS. Fine dry breadcrumbs, not panko. Panko gives a spikier, craggier crust that is good in its own right but is not this. Whichever you use, do not press them on.

MEAT. Pork loin is the standard here and is what Jagerschnitzel is made from. Veal makes it Wiener Schnitzel and wants a gentler hand and a shorter fry; chicken breast works and is the most forgiving of the three.

SPATZLE. Can be made ahead and held, then crisped in brown butter in a wide pan while the schnitzel is in the oven. Do that last, in the fat you have just been frying in if you like.

recipes.name: Best mushroom gravy
recipes.ingredients:
2 tablespoons butter, bacon grease, lard or beef drippings
1 yellow onion, finely chopped
1 clove garlic, minced
16 ounces fresh mushrooms, cleaned and sliced
1 tablespoon ground dried porcini mushrooms
4 tablespoons unsalted butter
4 tablespoons all-purpose flour
2 cups strong beef broth
1 teaspoon dark balsamic vinegar
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon sugar
1/4 teaspoon dried thyme
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons heavy cream, optional, for a creamy gravy
recipes.steps:
1. Melt the butter — or the bacon grease, lard or beef drippings, any of which will give more flavour — in a pan over medium-high heat and fry the onion until it begins to brown. Add the garlic and cook another minute.

2. Add the mushrooms and cook 7 to 8 minutes, until golden and the liquid they release has evaporated. Add the ground porcini and cook another minute.

3. Add the 4 tablespoons butter and melt it. Stir in the flour and cook about 3 minutes, stirring continually. This cooks off the raw flour and browns it, which is where the depth comes from.

4. Add the broth, vinegar, thyme, sugar, salt and pepper. Whisk continually until thickened, then cover and simmer on low 5 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season to taste. Thin with a little water, or with the cream if using.
recipes.notes:
The ground porcini is doing more work here than its one tablespoon suggests — it is most of why this tastes deeper than a standard mushroom gravy. If you only have dried porcini pieces, grind them in a spice grinder or pound them in a ziplock.

"Strong" beef broth is the source's word and it matters: add an extra teaspoon or two of beef base to ordinary broth. A weak broth makes a flat gravy that no amount of salt fixes.

GLUTEN FREE. Skip the flour step entirely. At the end, after the broth and seasonings are in, stir in a slurry of 1 tablespoon cornstarch dissolved in 2 tablespoons water and simmer a minute to thicken.

Makes enough for 6, so it covers 5 schnitzel with some left. It reheats well — make it before the cutlets and keep it warm, since once you start frying you will not want to be stirring a roux.

Serve it under the schnitzel or in a jug rather than poured over. Panko goes soft fast.
